title: Two in three of the Mayor’s contract notices were filed late; 186 came over a year late

beats.text: Two in three of the Mayor’s contract notices were filed late.

visual.sub: of the Mayor’s contract notices were filed late

beats.text: 186 came more than a year late, when the twelve months they support had already run.

visual.label: filed more than a year after the approval

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: A contract of 100,000 dollars or more needs a notice to the Ethics Commission.

visual.label: Contract-approval notice
visual.sub: filed with the Ethics Commission for approvals of $100,000 or more

beats.text: It names the contractor’s people, who may not give to that official’s campaign.

visual.label: The public list
visual.sub: the contractor, its officers and directors: who may not give

beats.text: The form says: file within five business days.

visual.text: must file this form with the Ethics Commission within five business days of approval

beats.text: The donor ban runs until twelve months after approval, or longer while negotiations go on.

visual.line: “until the later of either the termination of negotiations for such contract or twelve months after the date City approves the contract”

beats.text: Since January 2019,

visual.label: Mayor’s notices for approvals since January 2019 filed late (65.2%)

beats.text: the Mayor’s office filed 2,497 of its 3,830 notices late.

visual.label: Mayor’s notices for approvals since January 2019 filed late (65.2%)

beats.text: The Board’s Clerk files the same form, to the same deadline. Late on 8.4 percent.
For 2025 and 2026, 0.3 percent. The deadline can be met.

visual.sub: the Clerk’s notices filed late, approvals dated 2025 and 2026

beats.text: The Mayor’s share swings by year:

visual.kicker: Notices filed late, by year of approval: the Mayor’s and the Board’s

beats.text: 99.2 percent late for 2022, 98.7 for 2023.

visual.kicker: Notices filed late, by year of approval: the Mayor’s and the Board’s

beats.text: Then under a third in 2024 and 2025,

visual.kicker: Notices filed late, by year of approval: the Mayor’s and the Board’s

beats.text: and back up to 73.6 percent this year.

visual.kicker: Notices filed late, by year of approval: the Mayor’s and the Board’s

beats.text: The longest gap: an approval dated October 2021,
a notice signed January 2024.
838 days.
Of the 196 notices filed over a year late,

visual.label: Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development
visual.sub: filer’s department on 166 of the 196 notices filed over a year late

beats.text: 166 name the Mayor’s housing office as filer.

visual.label: Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development
visual.sub: filer’s department on 166 of the 196 notices filed over a year late

beats.text: Most were signed in batches: 69 of them in May 2023.
At the Retirement Board, all 169 notices were late, typically by 71 days.

visual.label: Retirement Board notices: every one late, typically by 71 days

beats.text: When every notice is late, the cause looks like the way they are routed.

visual.label: The routing?
visual.sub: where every notice is late, the cause looks like the way notices are routed

beats.text: Did barred money slip in? The screen finds just 2 donations in the gap: 500 dollars.

visual.sub: $500 in all, between an approval and its notice

beats.text: A late notice is the City office’s lapse. It says nothing about the contractor named on it.

visual.line: A late notice is a City office’s lapse and says nothing about the contractor or grantee named on it.

beats.text: Not known: why 2021 approvals were signed in 2024, or whether the Commission has looked.

cards: Why approvals dated 2021 were still being signed in 2024
Whether the typed date is the approval or the start of the grant
Whether the Ethics Commission has reviewed the lateness

beats.text: Staff turnover, bulk grant signings, or a new filing system may account for it.

visual.label: Other readings
visual.sub: staff turnover · grant agreements signed in bulk · a change of filing system in 2026

beats.text: What would settle it? The grant agreements’ signing dates, and any Commission review.

cards.what: The signing dates of the grant agreements behind the year-late notices
Any Ethics Commission review of late notices

beats.text: No one named here was contacted. No authority has made a finding on the lateness.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
